result.topic_en: Gauss introduces the lemniscatic sine and cosine (sn, cs) as inverse functions of the integral ∫dx/√(1−x⁴) and lists their basic relations, addition theorems, duplication formulas and values at multiples of ϖ/2; a block of numbers is written upside down in the margin.
result.transcription:
Math. 25
Elegantiores Integralis
$\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(1-x^4)}}$
proprietates.

Valorem huius integralis ab $x=0$ usque ad $x=1$ semper per
$\frac{1}{2}\varpi$ designamus. Variabilem $x$ respectu integralis per signum
sn. denotamus respectu vero [-differentiae-] complementi integralis
ad $\frac{1}{2}\varpi$, per cs. Ita ut $sn.\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^4}}=x$ ; $cs\left(\frac{1}{2}\varpi-\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{(1-x^4)}}\right)=x$.
Variabilis $x$ tamquam radius vector curvae; integrale autem
tamquam curvae arcus respondens considerari potest; curva vero
erit ea quam Lemniscatam dixerunt. Haec sufficiunt ad intel-
ligenda quae sequuntur.

$1=ss+cc+sscc$ sive $2=(1+ss)(1+cc)$
$s=\sqrt{\frac{1-cc}{1+cc}}$ ; $c=\sqrt{\frac{1-ss}{1+ss}}$
$sn.\, a\pm b=\frac{s.c'\pm s'.c}{1\mp scs'c'}$
$cs.\, a\pm b=\frac{cc'\mp ss'}{1\pm ss'cc'}$
$sn.\, 2a=\frac{2sc(1+ss)}{1+s^4}=\frac{2sc}{1-sscc}=\frac{2sc}{ss+cc}=\frac{2s\sqrt{(1-s^4)}}{1+s^4}$
$cs.\, 2a=\frac{cc-ss}{1+ccss}=\frac{cc-ss}{2-cc-ss}=\frac{1-2ss-s^4}{1+2ss-s^4}=\frac{1-2cc-c^4}{1+2cc-c^4}$
$\left.\begin{matrix}sin\\cos\end{matrix}\right\} k\varpi=\left\{\begin{matrix}0\\ \pm1\end{matrix}\right\}$ ; $\left.\begin{matrix}sin\\cos\end{matrix}\right\} k+\frac{1}{2}\varpi=\left\{\begin{matrix}\pm1\\0\end{matrix}\right\}$  $sin\,-a=-sin\, a$
$cos\,-a=cos\, a$
k denotante numerum integrum quemcunque positivum seu negativum
signum superius sumendum quoties k est par; inferius quoties est impar.

Expressing s in terms of c and vice versa
